reading.body:
This Aurora facility publishes 6.75 MW of critical load UPS capacity across 171,289 square feet, making it the second-largest facility by published capacity in Colorado. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this UPS capacity could support roughly 170 racks of compute, though the operator publishes no breakdown of actual IT load, tenant mix, or power delivery beyond the UPS tier. The facility holds certifications for regulated workloads: HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, and SSAE 18, qualifying it to host healthcare, payment, federal, and defense-adjacent operations.

Colorado has published capacity of 26.35 MW across three facilities that report figures to operator spec pages, with 17 mapped locations statewide. This Aurora site represents 25.6 percent of the state's published critical capacity, placing it second only to one other facility in the region.

What matters for AI scaling depends on questions the operator does not answer in published specs: total IT load separate from UPS capacity, actual power delivery infrastructure, electrical headroom, cooling capacity, and grid interconnection constraints. The certifications indicate a facility built for compliance-intensive workloads, not necessarily optimized for the sustained high-density compute that drives current AI model training.
